_about: A small FICTIONAL web used for offline mode. Every vendor, person, domain, certificate number and date is invented for teaching. All domains end in .example (a reserved TLD that can never be real). The pages are deliberately messy: a stale security page, a same-name company in another country, a forum rumour, a syndicated copy of a vendor page, a review site, and one page carrying a prompt-injection attack. `mock_claims` is what a well-behaved extraction LLM would pull from `text`; in offline mode the agent uses it instead of calling a model.

documents.title: Post-incident report: API token exposure, April 2025
documents.text: Post-incident report. On 14 April 2025 a logging misconfiguration caused API tokens for 212 customer workspaces to be written to an internal log store readable by a wider group of LedgerLens engineers than intended. No customer content was accessed. All affected tokens were rotated within six hours and affected customers were notified on 15 April. Root cause: a logging library upgrade changed the default redaction behaviour. Fixes: redaction tests added to CI, log store access reduced to the on-call team, token format changed to allow automatic detection in logs.

value.summary: API tokens for 212 workspaces written to an over-permissioned internal log store; tokens rotated within 6 hours; no customer content accessed
